Middle/bottom: lower/upper-bound 1σ credible intervals for the activity maps. More computationally intensive approaches to error estimates include Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) and bootstrapping. Both approaches have examined in a similar fashion as the example shown in Fig. 9 and result in error estimates that are more constrained than the Bayesian credible interval. The fractional decrease in the activity range of the error interval for MCMC is often approximately two- to three-fold (albeit not always). MCMC performs repeated random samples of the image space defined by the system matrix to produce statistical estimates of the covariances in the best-fit image space. Bootstrapping uses the assumption of Poisson statistics to re-sample forward projections of the best-fit image solution, which in turn is subject to the same LBNL Report #2001653 image solver (MLEM, MAP-EM, etc.), creating a set of solutions, whose variance is assumed to represent the true variance of the best-fit image. In our limited experience, bootstrapping is the most constrained answer to error estimation, but suffers from the very high level of computation necessary to achieve a representative answer. IterativeBayesianunfolding(IBU)[42]hasalsobeentestedagainstavarietyofdatasetsandwas found to have a performance between the Pereya algorithm and MCMC despite being even more computationally expensive. Efforts to produce robust and relevant error bounds in operationally relevant time-frames remains of interest as would be integration of such software into the real-time SDF framework. 2.3.3 Use of gamma-imaging techniques SDF algorithms have been coupled with both Compton and coded mask imaging techniques, often within the same LAMP detector system [26]. Such coupling for coded mask imaging only requires knowledge of the per-detector efficiency functions (ϵ (Ω) in Eqs. 1/2), whereas Compton imaging requires both that information for each interaction d sequence, the capability within the data acquisition system (DAQ) to log coincident interaction events, and more sophisticated reconstruction algorithms that accurately account for event selection, Compton uncertainties, and the nature of coincident events. The incorporation of Compton uncertainties for voxelized reconstructions was the subject of study that culminated recently in Ref. [43]. Compton SDF also typically leverages the ‘list-mode’ formulation of Eq. 1.
